buckets.title: Hybridisation as a bounded orbital model
buckets.badge_reason: The hard move is not recalling sp/sp2/sp3 labels; it is deciding when local counting is adequate and what orbital/model evidence warrants beyond it.

capabilities.action: Use local hybridisation language conditionally, test orbital alignment/connectivity, and keep qualitative model variables separate from stronger physical claims
capabilities.success_criterion: The learner can execute the supplied model, identify its warranted inference, reject a causal/quantitative overclaim, and state what additional evidence/model would be needed.

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Resolve conflict between a local Lewis inventory and supplied aligned delocalisation.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: A hybrid label describes a chosen basis; it does not independently cause donation.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Account for sigma framework, donor orientation and adjacent pi acceptor before qualifying the label.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Approximately planar amide N can use an introductory sp2-like sigma framework plus an aligned p-like lone-pair donor. Four Lewis entries do not override the supplied delocalised-model conditions; the basis is not unique observed reality.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Remove the hybridisation label: the alignment-plus-acceptor explanation must still describe the supplied donation condition.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Compare adjacent amide N with a saturated-spacer amine N. Does the same four-entry Lewis inventory establish the same donation pathway?
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: No. Adjacency/alignment conditions differ. Repeating automatic four-domains-therefore-localized-sp3 in both exposes applicability failure.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Give one observation that constrains the model and one claim it cannot uniquely prove.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: Four Lewis entries overrule supplied delocalisation conditions.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q1

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Construct both arrangements while preserving connectivity and electron inventories.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: Torsion changes relative orientation, not the number of atoms or formal electrons.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Draw a fixed carbonyl reference and an N donor direction rotated about the declared C-N axis.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Formamide CH3NO has 18 valence electrons and 24 total electrons. The supplied three-centre donor/carbonyl pi model has four electrons. A 90-degree twist changes alignment, not these inventories.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Independent element sums: valence 4+3+5+6=18; total 6+3+7+8=24. Both sketches must preserve them.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Count valence and total electrons for CH3NO before and after torsion. Identify which geometric relation changes.
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: 18 valence, 24 total in both; relative donor direction changes. Repeated electron-loss-by-rotation reasoning differs from a corrected addition slip.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Sketch a fixed-connectivity 45-degree comparison without claiming measured donation.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: Torsion changes the formal electron inventory.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q2

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Explain the supplied trend without replacing a mechanism with a label.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: Relative donor/acceptor alignment is a model variable; donation magnitude needs additional physics.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Connect changed geometry to overlap, then tag each statement as given, model or observation.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Twisting reduces relevant alignment and the supplied delocalisation contribution. A changing hybrid label alone explains neither mechanism nor a quantitative barrier; total torsional energy has additional contributions.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Counterfactual: remove the word hybridisation while retaining changed orientation; the mechanistic statement survives.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: If two sketches have the same label but different donor alignment, must their donation be identical? If the label changes alone, has a mechanism been supplied?
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: Neither follows. Persistent label-only explanations expose causal substitution.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: State which additional model would be needed for a numerical donation or barrier estimate.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: A changed hybrid label is a causal explanation of donor strength.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q3

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Build a decision procedure that can fail its own applicability test.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: Local count and a continuous aligned pathway are independent checks.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Test locality, adjacency, alignment and stated model conditions; invent a structural counterfactual yourself.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Amide A has the supplied direct donor/carbonyl path. Saturated-spacer amine B lacks that ordinary contiguous path. Spatial proximity alone is insufficient, and absence of this path is not an absolute zero-interaction theorem.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed case: replace a saturated interruption by a suitably aligned unsaturated bridge; reassess connectivity and orbital availability rather than reusing the answer.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Would folding the saturated-spacer molecule closer create the same continuous p pathway as removing the spacer?
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: No; spatial folding and orbital-connected adjacency are different changes. Repeated proximity-based classification identifies the wrong criterion.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Specify a counterfactual bridge and test all procedure conditions again.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: Spatial proximity equals an orbital-connected p pathway.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q4

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Test uniqueness, rather than merely finding one familiar angle.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: Several shapes/angles can share an introductory four-domain classification.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Use supplied counterexamples and the amide boundary to qualify both predictive scope and evidence.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: CH4/NH3/H2O share common sp3-like introductory descriptions while their nuclear shapes/angles differ. Geometry constrains models but does not uniquely measure a hybrid decomposition; lone pairs and delocalisation matter.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Independent counterexample: a shared four-domain label is compatible with 4,3,2 bonded-atom positions, so it cannot alone uniquely specify atom-only shape.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Can one four-domain label predict the same nuclear shape for CH4 and H2O? Does observing a shape uniquely establish an orbital basis?
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: No to both. Persistent one-label-one-shape or unique-basis inference reveals overclaim rather than an angle-recall slip.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Name evidence needed before claiming a unique physical electronic description.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: A hybrid label uniquely determines every angle and physical orbital basis.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q5

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Distinguish recalling a rule from establishing its applicability.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: Local counting assumes the localized/domain model is useful for the asked task.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: List the conditions and look for supplied delocalisation or unusual occupancy evidence before applying the shortcut.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Four-domain counting is useful for localized introductory classification. Adjacent pi acceptors, aligned donor orbitals, planarity/donation evidence or radical occupancy can require a richer model.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: the same formal lone-pair entry at an amine and an amide can have different orbital-role descriptions under the supplied conditions.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Both sites have three sigma bonds and a lone pair. Is that alone sufficient to choose identical localized orbital-role descriptions?
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: No; supplied adjacency/alignment evidence differs. Repeated rule use without checking conditions exposes applicability confusion.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Separate a recalled count from a model-selection decision in a new conjugated case.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: Recalling a local rule proves its applicability.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q6

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Translate occupancy as well as geometry in the supplied radical model.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: A singly occupied orbital is not an empty orbital or a lone pair.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Inventory the sigma electrons and remaining electron before drawing the p-like direction.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Supplied planar CH3 radical has three sigma directions and a perpendicular p-like SOMO with one electron. Three sigma bonds alone do not determine an empty residual p orbital.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Independent count: CH3 radical has 4+3=7 valence electrons; three sigma pairs use six, leaving one.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Compare CH3 radical (7 valence electrons) with a model CH3+ inventory (6). Must their residual p occupancy be the same?
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: No: one versus zero in these supplied local models. Repeating empty p for both reveals bonds-only occupancy inference.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Sketch the given radical while explicitly marking the singly occupied orbital.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: Three sigma bonds always imply an empty residual p orbital.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q7

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Separate a discriminating observation from the strength of the inference it warrants.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: A measurement can constrain multiple models without uniquely selecting an orbital decomposition.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: For each proposed observation write prediction, alternatives, conditions and inference limit.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Planarity/bond metrics and condition-specific spectroscopic/dynamic evidence can test localized versus delocalised accounts. Geometry alone does not uniquely measure donation, hybrid coefficients or a rotational barrier; exact empirical numbers need species/conditions/source.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Use two compatible electronic descriptions of a planar structure as a counterexample to geometry-implies-unique-orbitals.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Does observed planar geometry alone measure donor strength? What extra information would a numerical rotational barrier require?
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: No; a specified experiment or calculation and conditions/model are needed. Repeating direct geometry-to-strength inference exposes overinterpretation.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Design a second independent observation and state one alternative explanation.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: Geometry alone uniquely measures donation and a rotational barrier.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q8

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Execute the supplied cosine model and separately test the total-energy inference.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: An overlap factor is not an energy Hamiltonian or the whole energy budget.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Compute the three factors, then identify an independent energy term that the input does not constrain.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Given factors at 0,60,90 degrees are 1,1/2,0. Both cosine and cosine-squared are even. A degenerate two-orbital Hamiltonian with coupling t0 cos(theta) gives epsilon ± |t0 cos(theta)|, so no universal cosine-squared total-energy law follows.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: At theta=60 degrees the factor is fixed at 1/2 while adding an independently specified energy contribution changes total energy. This falsifies uniqueness without modelling formamide quantitatively.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: If theta stays at 60 degrees while an independent energy term changes, does overlap change? Does total energy necessarily stay fixed?
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: Overlap factor unchanged; total energy need not remain fixed. Repeated equality of overlap and total energy identifies variable conflation.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: State assumptions needed for a weak-coupling second-order squared-interaction estimate.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: The given overlap factor is the total molecular energy.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q9

grade9v3:question_repairs.clarify: Audit a proposed universal rule across cases that stress different boundaries.
grade9v3:question_repairs.connect: Counts, orbital roles, geometry and physical evidence are distinct layers.
grade9v3:question_repairs.way: Use NH3, allene, amide and separated amine as tests; retain a conditional framework rather than another universal slogan.
grade9v3:question_repairs.rule: Use local count as a bounded starting model, then check residual p directions, occupancy, adjacency/alignment and evidence. A label alone explains neither every geometry nor all reactivity. NH3, allene and amide stress different limitations.
grade9v3:question_repairs.check: Changed check: apply the framework to CH3 radical; three bonds plus one unpaired electron require an occupancy step absent from the original slogan.
grade9v3:question_repairs.probe: Would one bond/lone-pair count plus a label explain NH3 shape, allene terminal-plane relation and amide donation by the same mechanism?
grade9v3:question_repairs.pattern: No; their explanatory jobs differ. Repeating label-as-final-cause across all cases exposes an overgeneralised framework.
grade9v3:question_repairs.transfer: Produce a qualified procedure with an explicit stop-and-seek-more-evidence branch.
grade9v3:question_repairs.wrong_idea: A local count and label explain every geometry and reactivity difference.
grade9v3:question_repairs.label: Q10

microtopics.title: When a hybridisation label stops being the answer
microtopics.badge_reason: The learner already knows labels; the new work is evaluating applicability, orbital alignment and evidence scope.
entry_assumptions: Can distinguish sigma and pi overlap.
microtopics.inferential_jump: A local count can be a useful first model without being a complete physical explanation: structural connectivity and orbital alignment decide whether a delocalisation-sensitive model is needed, and a formula only warrants claims about the quantity it actually defines.

teaching_path.action: Separate three questions: what is counted locally, what orbitals can align, and what quantity the model actually predicts.
teaching_path.why_valid: Each question has a different evidence base; merging them creates the benchmark's main misconceptions.

teaching_path.action: Hold formamide connectivity/electron count fixed while changing only C-N torsional alignment.
teaching_path.why_valid: This isolates orbital orientation from Lewis bookkeeping.

teaching_path.action: For the supplied cos(theta) factor, compute only the named overlap quantity before evaluating any total-energy claim.
teaching_path.why_valid: A defined functional form cannot be silently transferred to another system quantity.

exit_task.prompt: A model says an orbital-overlap factor is 0.5 at one geometry. A classmate concludes that the molecule's total electronic energy is therefore half its reference value. What is warranted, what is not, and what extra information would be needed?

answer.summary: Only the overlap-factor statement is warranted from the supplied relation; the total-energy ratio is not determined.
reasoning: Name the quantity actually defined by the model.
Check whether any relation from overlap factor to total energy was supplied.
Request a specified energetic model or independent calculation/measurement before making the energy claim.
answer.check: The conclusion should remain valid even if another energy contribution changes while the same overlap factor is held fixed.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: No total-energy number follows from the overlap factor alone.

microtopics.research_contribution: Issue #37 clusters amide, radical and teaching-rule questions around one transferable skill: use orbital models conditionally and police the boundary between a model variable and a stronger physical claim.

predict.prompt: At theta = 0°, 60° and 90°, what values does the supplied cos(theta) overlap-factor model give? Before revealing anything else, decide whether those three values also determine total molecular energy.
predict.defensible_answer: The overlap-factor values can be calculated; the total-energy claim needs a separate relation.

attempt.produces: Three overlap-factor predictions plus a written yes/no judgement on the total-energy claim and one sentence naming missing evidence.

rubric.criterion: Keeps cos(theta) attached to the overlap factor.
rubric.evidence_of: Executes the given model without transferring its functional form to total energy.
Understands model scope rather than merely rejecting the claim.

accepted: 1, 1/2, 0 for overlap; total-energy law underdetermined without another model.
rejected: Energy must be 1, 1/2, 0 because overlap is.

task.prompt: Compute overlap-factor values, then audit the energy claim.

route.ask: What noun immediately follows the supplied formula in the question?
route.why_this_ask: It binds the formula to the overlap factor.

route.ask: Where is an energy-vs-overlap equation supplied?
route.why_this_ask: Its absence exposes the unsupported bridge.

route.ask: Could another energy contribution vary while theta stays fixed?
route.why_this_ask: It tests whether total energy is underdetermined by overlap alone.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: The learner reconstructs the evidence boundary from the claim itself rather than memorising a warning.

boundary_test.prompt: If a later problem explicitly supplies E(theta)=E0+A cos²(theta), may you then calculate its energy-angle dependence?
boundary_test.answer: Yes, within that supplied energetic model and its stated conditions; that still does not make the Q9 total-energy law cos(theta).
boundary_test.confirms: Model scope depends on the defined quantity and relation, not on a ban against mathematical models.

construction_units.decision: Execute a supplied orbital model while preventing an unsupported transfer from overlap to total energy

independent_checks.statement: Remove the hybridisation label: the alignment-plus-acceptor explanation must still describe the supplied donation condition.
Give one observation that constrains the model and one claim it cannot uniquely prove.

compact_anchor.prompt: What does the model actually define?
compact_anchor.result: Execute that relation, then stop unless a second relation/evidence warrants the stronger claim.

relations.expression: supplied overlap factor = cos(theta); model scope does not automatically extend to total molecular energy
relations.meaning: A mathematical relation is evidence only about the quantity it defines. At 0°, 60° and 90° the supplied overlap-factor values are 1, 1/2 and 0; a total-energy law requires an additional energetic model or evidence.

symbols.meaning: angle between the supplied orbital-alignment directions

conditions: Use the relation only for the overlap factor named in Q9.
Keep atom connectivity and formal electron count distinct from orbital orientation in the torsion comparison.
Do not infer donation magnitude or total molecular energy without an additional specified relation/model.

derivation.action: Name the exact quantity the supplied formula describes.
derivation.why_valid: This prevents a functional form from being transferred to a different physical quantity.

derivation.action: Evaluate the supplied relation only for the requested angles.
derivation.why_valid: This executes the model without adding assumptions.

derivation.action: Ask whether any independent energy-vs-overlap relation was supplied.
derivation.why_valid: Without that bridge, the total-energy functional form is underdetermined.

limits: The cosine rule is a benchmark-supplied simplified overlap model, not a measured complete electronic-structure Hamiltonian.
Hybridisation labels are descriptive model vocabulary and do not by themselves cause delocalisation or geometry.
checks: For every conclusion, point to the prompt-given relation, an authored model assumption, or an external evidence source.

representations.purpose: Construct local directions in an explicitly declared end-on projection; preserve connectivity, occupancy and model limits.
instance_constraints: The first stage must not reveal the Q9 protected conclusion.
No visual element may imply measured donation strength or a total-energy curve.
accessibility: SVG has title, description and text equivalents for orientation changes.
No meaning is encoded by colour alone.
misleading_alternatives: Changing Lewis electron count when twisting the C-N bond.
Drawing a total-energy cosine curve as if it were supplied evidence.

correspondence.in_words: Line style, labels and the declared end-on view distinguish the local directions.

demand_dimensions.model_choice: Choose whether local counting is sufficient or whether an orbital-alignment/model-boundary analysis is required.
demand_dimensions.representation_translation: Translate connectivity and torsion into orbital alignment without altering formal electron count.
demand_dimensions.reasoning_steps: Classify assumptions, execute model, critique overclaim, transfer framework.
demand_dimensions.novelty: Amide, radical, allene and evidence/model-boundary cases beyond routine label recall.

safe_variations: Change the angle or separate-site connectivity while preserving an explicit statement of what model relation is supplied.
transfer_boundaries: Do not infer conjugation from spatial proximity alone.
Do not infer a whole-system energy law from an overlap-factor formula alone.
common_wrong_routes: Treat a hybridisation label as a cause.
Promote a qualitative sketch into a measurement.
